dedupe_keys.name: ipis open data on artisanal and small scale mining sites eastern drc central african republic tanzania zimbabwe

description: IPIS, a Belgian research institute, publishes the results of its field visits to artisanal and small-scale mining sites as open data. The eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo file downloaded on 26 September 2026 had 7,163 visits to about 3,400 sites between 2009 and December 2025, and the Central African Republic file 914 visits to 360 sites (2019 to 2021). Each visit records location and administrative units, number of workers, access in dry and wet season, whether the site is a tin, tantalum, tungsten or gold mine, up to three minerals with selling points and final destinations, mercury use, and the presence, taxation and other interference of armed groups or state actors; the CAR file adds women and child workers and services. HDX also lists IPIS visit data for north-west Tanzania (2017 to 2019) and the Runde river valley in Zimbabwe (2019). Data are free under the Open Data Commons Attribution Licence 1.0, as CSV or GeoJSON, with a dashboard, webmap, data dictionary and tutorial. Caveats: the IPIS geoserver is offline during a database migration, so only direct CSV links for DRC and CAR work; visits are samples; and IPIS may delay release by up to six months. For simulation it maps the artisanal mineral supply chain in conflict areas, useful for tin, tantalum, tungsten and gold supply risk and access road disruption studies. Related catalogue records include the USGS Mineral Resources Data System and the WRI mining concessions layer.
